title: The Drowned Sigil
premise: Mirabel Villalobos, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics he carves, has spent years keeping the ledgers of the Gilded Meridian, a guild that trades in impossible things while erasing its own history. When the crown's witch-hunters burn a neighboring district and post bounties for 'the gifted,' Mirabel learns his guildmaster sold his name to save her own. Fleeing with a ledger that proves the crown itself was built on stolen magic, he must find the Drowned Sigil—a door out of Vessany, a country whose true borders were drowned and erased from every map. In the end, Mirabel chooses not escape but exposure: he reads the ledger aloud to the dead, letting their testimony unmake the crown's legitimacy, though it costs him his hearing and leaves him, finally, only himself.
about_author: Quentin Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of books that officially never existed. He writes fantasy from a coastal town where the tide charts are famously unreliable.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. While carving a relic for a client, he hears a dead woman accuse the guild of selling her name to the crown's hunters. He confronts guildmaster Odile Ferrant, who coolly reveals his own name is already on the bounty list—payment for her amnesty. Emotional beat: betrayal and the shattering of his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, intercut with the voice of a drowned cartographer in an old bone compass. Hunted through the flooded lowquarters, he deciphers the ledger's hidden marginalia: the Drowned Sigil, a door at the heart of old Vessany, sealed when the crown erased the country's true history. Emotional beat: desperate hope entangled with grief for the life he's losing.

chapters.title: What the Dead Testify
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Mirabel and hunter-sergeant Cassian Roe, who begins doubting the hunt as he reads confiscated ledgers. Mirabel reaches the sunken archive beneath the old capital, where the dead crowd him with their unfinished accounts—and Odile arrives to take the ledger back by force. Emotional beat: rising dread as justice and survival become the same impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Mirabel's POV closing with Cassian's. At the Drowned Sigil, Mirabel refuses the door; instead he opens the ledger and reads the dead's testimony aloud as the sigil floods the city with remembered truth. The crown's claim dissolves; Odile drowns in her own debts. The gift leaves him silent—but Cassian stays to help rebuild what the reading uncovered. Emotional beat: costly, quiet triumph.
